_comment: REAL measured baseline from a physical Dell Z9100-ON, read over console from Dell OS9 9.14(2.24) BEFORE the SONiC install. This is ground truth for calibrating the modeled energy/thermal curves in app/collector/fabric_exporter.py, so the model can be checked against real hardware.
source: Dell OS9 console: show inventory / show environment / show system brief

idle_state._comment: No traffic, no optics installed, switch idle ~40min after boot

model_calibration_notes: IDLE POWER = 143 W measured. Before 2026-08 the exporter's switch model used 180 + intensity*220 W, so its idle floor (180 W) overstated real idle by ~26%. It now uses 145 + intensity*255 W.

Bcm56960 is the Tomahawk-1 ASIC die sensor and reads 37 C at idle; Bcm_Int reads 55 C. The exporter's ASIC_WARN=62 / ASIC_CRIT=72 thresholds are therefore plausible but should be re-baselined against whichever sensor SONiC exposes.
Fans idle at ~6100-6460 RPM across 5 trays. The exporter models 6000 + max(0, asic-45)*350, which matches the idle floor well.
These are OS9 readings. After the SONiC install, re-read via PMON/STATE_DB and diff - any delta is a NOS reporting difference, not a hardware change.
